population_note: The de facto authorities' estimate of the people present on 1 January 2026: their census of February 2011, carried forward with each year's births and arrivals added and deaths and departures taken away (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.11). Georgia's own 2014 census and Geostat's estimates do not cover Abkhazia, and the authorities that count it are recognised by few states.
ethnicity_note: Nationality as the de facto authorities' census of February 2011 counted it (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.12), Georgians and Mingrelians apart as the census lists them. Their tables for later years, to 1 January 2026, keep each district's 2011 shares to within a fifth of a percentage point, so they are not a newer count.
median_age_note: Interpolated within the five-year age group holding the middle person, from the de facto authorities' census of February 2011 (their statistics committee's yearbook, table 1.2). Their age tables for later years print the 2011 census's shares against each year's total, so they carry nothing newer.

population.note: The de facto authorities redrew the districts here after the war: in 1995 they formed Tkvarcheli district from parts of the Ochamchira and Gal districts, and they count more of Gal's former villages in Ochamchira district. The outlines drawn as Ochamchire and Gali are the districts as they were before, so neither holds a district the authorities count: villages of the Ochamchira and Tkvarcheli districts lie in this one, and Gal's villages along the Enguri, such as Otobaia, lie outside it, in the outline drawn as Zugdidi. Ochamchira, Tkvarcheli and Gal districts together had 72,882 people on 1 January 2026 (26,073, 16,458 and 30,351); no figure is written for either outline.
